subject: Re: Packaging proposal — gradual tier taper & component bundling
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@medimatics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging proposal: gradual tier taper option for Medimatics

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the call today. Based on your feedback about predictable spend and avoiding sudden feature regressions if you need to step down tiers, we sketched an alternative: a "gradual tier taper" approach that soft-degrades non-critical capabilities over a short transition window rather than removing them immediately. The goal is to make downgrades low-friction for Medimatics while protecting unit economics.

High level:
- 30–90 day taper window after a tier downgrade where the most expensive features (dedicated KV cache, auto-batching burst) are throttled gradually rather than cut.
- Credits applied pro rata for the remaining duration of the billing commitment when a downgrade is requested mid-term.
- Two bundled offerings: "Full" (includes all features), "Tapered" (same base entitlements but with a taper schedule for premium features).

What we'd like from you:
1) Confirmation that a 60-day pilot taper is acceptable as a starting point.
2) A prioritized list of the top 3 features you consider "must-have" during a downgrade (e.g., prefix caching, real-time KV cache, region pinning).
3) Procurement's timeline for a contract amendment if we include a taper clause.

I've attached a first-pass pricing matrix and a sample taper schedule. Ben/Marissa, looping you in to keep this aligned with existing discounts and the pricing band we discussed.

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (internal), taper_schedule_v1.xlsx (internal)

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@medimatics.com>

Subject: Re: Packaging proposal: gradual tier taper option for Medimatics

Dylan —

Appreciate the thoughtful approach. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Procurement will need a clear credit formula and examples (if we step down after 4 months of a 12-month commit, how many credits and how are premium features prorated?).
- For compliance/regulatory reasons, we cannot have any invisibly degraded observability (we need auditing during the taper). Are you able to guarantee full audit logs during the taper window?
- Top 3 must-haves during a downgrade: 1) audit logs & tracing, 2) region pinning, 3) prefix KV cache for session continuity.

Can you provide a one-page comparison table: immediate downgrade vs 60-day taper vs 90-day taper, with 
- list of features maintained,
- cost impact to Medimatics (example numbers),
- credit applied, and
- SLA changes (if any).

Procurement: we need to target an amendment review next week (w/e 2026-08-09) — can your team get the details to legal/procurement by end of day 2026-08-03?

Thanks,

Sophie
Director of Platform Engineering | Medimatics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@medimatics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging proposal: gradual tier taper option for Medimatics

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick response to each point and a concrete proposal below.

1) Credit formula (example):
- If you downgrade mid-term, we calculate unused committed capacity (in token-equivalents) and apply a pro rata credit equal to the remaining months on the commitment less a 10% operational transition fee. Example: 12-month $120k commit downgraded after month 4 -> remaining value $80k; credit = $80k * 0.9 = $72k applied to future invoices or as a one-time credit.

2) Audit logs: we confirm full audit log retention and access during the taper window. Logs live in your VPC/Workspace and are unaffected by feature throttles.

3) One-page comparison table: attached. It includes immediate vs 60d vs 90d taper columns with feature states, sample cost delta, and example credit.

Proposed taper schedule (summary):
- Day 0–14: No change (grace stabilization).
- Day 15–45: Non-critical burst/batching scaled to 70% of prior capacity.
- Day 46–90: Further scale to 40% and remove dedicated burst capacity after day 90.

Pilot recommendation: start with a 60-day taper for the initial rollout with the option to extend to 90 days for enterprise customers. We recommend a 30% discount on the taper period for impacted features (reflected in the attached taper_schedule_v1.xlsx).

Attachments: taper_schedule_v1.xlsx (schedule + numbers), one_page_comparison.pdf (comparison table)

Ben Carter
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Sophie —

Thanks — great alignment. Quick recap and next steps so procurement has what they need by Monday: 

Agreement in principle:
- Start with a 60-day taper as the standard downgrade path; optional 90-day taper for enterprise accounts.
- Audit logs remain available and untouched during taper.
- Credit formula: pro rata remaining value less 10% transition fee (Ben's example).
- Pilot discount on tapered features: 30% during taper window.

Deliverables we will send by EOD 2026-08-03:
- One-page comparison (immediate / 60d / 90d) — attached (one_page_comparison.pdf).
- Taper schedule with example numbers for your 12-month case (taper_schedule_v1.xlsx).
- Draft amendment language for legal/procurement to review (Lauren, can you shepherd the draft to Procurement and Legal? Happy to run a quick call with your counsel if helpful.)

Sophie, can you confirm procurement's preferred time for a 30-minute review on 2026-08-04 or 2026-08-05? If we can lock a slot, we will have Ben and Lauren on the call.

Next steps for Redwood (internal): Ben/Marissa, prep the HubSpot deal record and update the pricing grid to lock these items. Lauren, I marked this as a matter for legal review (amendment + SLA note).

Thanks all — looking forward to closing this in the week.
